headline: Learned models conditioned on structure and biological context drive molecular design
label: Machine Learning Molecular Design
summary: Pretrained sequence and structure models are being adapted via preference optimization and conditional generation for design tasks.
synthesis: The dominant thread is conditioning learned sequence and structure models on biological context. AbRefine couples backbone-conditioned structural predictions with framework-conditioned antibody language model distributions, and ParaEM predicts paratope residues from antibody and antigen sequences using ESM3 embeddings. Several designs adapt pretrained models: SimBinder-IF tunes only the decoder of frozen ESM-IF via SimPO, and PolyTamGen applies DPO to ESM3 target embeddings. Generative and contrastive methods extend this to pocket-conditioned 3D generation, linker-conditioned PROTAC diffusion, and enzyme kcat prediction. A leakage audit of enzyme-substrate prediction serves as a counterpoint, showing that similarity-driven leakage inflates reported performance. The set is heterogeneous, so this is the dominant rather than universal pattern.
